The key factor in converting the sequential algorithm into a parallel one is the decomposition of the rational (fractional) approximation into simpler, independent components. By expressing the rational approximation as a sum of linear partial fractions, each term corresponds to solving a linear system with a shifted matrix. These systems are independent of one another and can be solved simultaneously across multiple processors, enabling parallelism. The other options (complex roots, nonlocal boundary conditions, stability analysis) do not directly provide the mechanism for parallel execution.

Answer: D
